I am 63 years old, my knees ache in the cold, and my husband passed three years ago. My son works in Shijiazhuang. I farm our 6 mu myself, with help from my neighbor's family at harvest time.

I have grown wheat and corn on this land for forty years. My mother grew wheat and corn before me. The soil here is clay-loam, it holds water if I am careful. I do not read — I learn from watching and from talking to neighbors at the village store.

This year I will do the same as always: winter wheat on all 6 mu, then summer maize on the same land after harvest. I cannot grow vegetables because I have no one to watch them carefully and the market in town is far. Cotton prices are bad and I do not know how to deal with the buyers anymore.

For wheat, I will buy Jimai seeds from the village supply cooperative — same as last year, they are the improved ones, not the hybrid, because I keep some back each year. I will apply compound fertilizer as base, then urea at jointing stage, same as my neighbor Old Wang's wife does. I will irrigate before winter sets in, again at jointing, at heading, and once more if it looks dry at grain fill — four times as usual. I spray herbicide in spring and once more for aphids if I see them.

For corn, I will buy hybrid seed — everyone buys hybrid now, the yields are much better. My son paid for the seed last year. After wheat harvest I will have the rotary tiller man come through once, then plant immediately. I will irrigate twice if there is no rain. One spray for fall armyworm, which has been bad lately.
